reviews.review:
TLDR: this feels more like an expansion to CRDM3 rather than a standalone game, do not expect something as long as the original game going in, and you'll probably have a great time. If you haven't played CRDM3, go play that first, then come back for this one


I enjoyed this game, it was fun and a nice little story in this neat little world Strange Scaffold carved out in CRDM3. But i do feel like i've been left having gotten less than i wanted out of this game. It felt like the game was winding down for its ending just around the point where it started to really get going.

While the same great gameplay is there, with a (i feel) heightened difficulty that is very appreciated, I do lament the loss of the maze-like feeling exploring the mansion had in CRDM3. It's a much more linear game, to the point where i have a bit of trouble calling it a Metroidvania like its predecessor.

Story is nice, more character focused this time and has some funny moments loaded in the chamber you'll no doubt enjoy if you're at all interested in game development or how games are made. I also want to give massive props to the soundtrack, which i believe far exceeds CRDM3's OST. Great job on that

The last point i want to make is that, while i've been negative in parts of this review, this game more than anything feels like a proof of concept for the game share program that Strange Scaffold is attempting, where they hand over the project files of finished project to another indie team to take a crack at making a game with those assets. In that respect, i think this attempt is quite a success, iterating on what made the first game great in a new way. I hope that more devs try out this idea so we can have more good, quality games out there without putting their developers in dangerous situations.

Congratulations on the release, looking forward to whatever you guys do next!
